title: Density and per-unit quotients (including working backward)
subtitle: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units · 12 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **12 of the official questions in Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units are this one** — 2 Easy, 5 Medium, 5 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The word 'density' or 'per square mile' or 'per cubic centimeter' appears.
- The question gives a count or mass plus an area or volume.
- Harder versions give the density and the mass and ask for a dimension (such as the edge of a cube).
- Others hide a subtraction, for example total area minus water area to get land area.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Density = amount ÷ space (mass ÷ volume, people ÷ land area).
- 2) If the density is given, rearrange: space = amount ÷ density.
- 3) If the question wants a length, take the square root of the area or the cube root of the volume.
- First check whether the area or volume needs adjusting, such as land only.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: It helps in the backward version.
Type x^3 = mass/density (or graph y = x^3 and y = mass/density) and read the positive intersection, which gives you the cube root without algebra.
For forward density it's just a calculator.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You flip the quotient (space ÷ amount).
That answer is usually one of the choices.
Other traps: using the total area when the question says land area, or stopping at the volume and not taking the cube root to get the edge length.

sections.heading: You are losing these
